questions.scenario: Your best friend is feeling very sad and low today. How do you help them?

options.text: Sit with them and listen carefully to their feelings.
Make them a healthy, tasty comfort meal to boost their mood.
Give them a nice shoulder and neck massage to release tension.
Take them to a quiet place, play soft music, and help them breathe.
Take them out for a run or a heavy workout session to sweat out the stress and release endorphins.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you could have a 'Healing Superpower', what would you choose?

options.text: The power to erase people's deep sadness and trauma.
The power to magically turn any junk food into super healthy food.
The power to instantly fix broken bones and muscle pains with a touch.
The power to instantly calm anyone's angry or stressful energy.
The power to give anyone unlimited physical stamina and perfect athletic strength.
None of these.

questions.scenario: It's your school's Sports Day. What is your role behind the scenes?

options.text: Motivating the players who are feeling nervous before the game.
Mixing the exact energy and hydration drinks for the team.
Helping players stretch properly and fixing their muscle cramps.
Leading a 5-minute silent meditation so the team focuses better.
Leading the intense warm-up drills and aggressively pumping up the team's energy.
None of these.

questions.scenario: What kind of short videos (Reels/Shorts) do you enjoy watching the most?

options.text: 'How to read body language' or 'Psychology facts'.
'Healthy zero-sugar snacks' or 'What I eat in a day'.
'Fix your neck posture in 5 minutes' or 'Satisfying bone cracking'.
'Morning Yoga routines' or 'Peaceful nature sounds'.
'High-intensity home workout routines' or 'Insane gym transformations'.
None of these.

questions.scenario: When you are personally very stressed, what makes you feel better?

options.text: Writing my thoughts in a diary or talking to someone.
Drinking herbal tea and eating light, clean food.
Doing deep stretches to crack my stiff joints.
Sitting alone in silence, closing my eyes, and meditating.
Going for a fast run, lifting weights, or doing an intense sweaty workout.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Which of these everyday problems fascinates you to solve?

options.text: Why do people overthink and get anxiety?
How do different vitamins actually change our skin and energy?
How do bones, muscles, and nerves work together like a machine?
How does breathing connect our mind, body, and soul?
How the body builds muscle, burns fat, and increases physical endurance.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Your older relative comes to you with a complaint. Who do you want to help first?

options.text: An aunt who is feeling lonely and depressed.
An uncle who is struggling to control his sugar and weight.
A grandparent whose knees hurt when they walk.
A cousin who is restless, angry, and has no peace of mind.
A cousin who wants to get fit, build stamina, and start training for a marathon.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Every healing job requires patience. Which of these 'boring' tasks can you do happily?

options.text: Listening to a person cry about the same problem 10 times without judging.
Calculating calories, proteins, and designing strict food charts daily.
Helping a patient do the exact same slow physical exercise for 3 months.
Waking up at 4 AM every single day for silent disciplined practice.
Tracking reps and sets, and constantly pushing someone who wants to give up during a workout.
None of these.

questions.scenario: You want to gift something to a very stressed friend. What do you buy?

options.text: A beautiful self-care journal for them to write their feelings.
A basket of exotic healthy fruits and detox drinks.
A high-quality muscle massager or foam roller.
A Himalayan salt lamp, incense sticks, and a yoga mat.
A set of resistance bands, adjustable dumbbells, or a gym membership.
None of these.

questions.scenario: In your friend group, what title suits you best?

options.text: The Therapist (The one who listens and gives life advice).
The Health Freak (The one who checks what everyone is eating).
The Mechanic (The one who cracks backs and knows posture tricks).
The Zen Master (The one who is always calm and unbothered).
The Coach / Gym Bro (The one who always talks about working out and staying active).
None of these.
